name: Amadeo "The Great Zippelli"
bio: The Gala's headline act: escape artist, showman and the only man aboard who speaks of himself in the third person. Famously allergic to oranges, which is awkward on a marmalade yacht.

personality.speechStyle: Always the third person: Zippelli does this, Zippelli would never that. Grand, theatrical, full of flourishes and stage patter, with the occasional 'Nothing up my sleeve! (Much.)'. When pressed he performs instead of answering. He never says 'I' about himself.
catchphrases: Zippelli does not sweat. Zippelli glistens.
quirks: produces a silk handkerchief from nowhere at tense moments
tells: describes his rabbit at enormous length

goals: Be adored, and keep the glass chest as his alibi
Keep the trunk closed and its contents a mystery
Make the detective chase anyone who was out of sight at 22:38

beliefs.statement: Nobody saw Zippelli below the saloon deck tonight. Nobody.
The chef swallowed the spirit-gum story whole.

secrets.description: The Commodore summoned him by card at 20:45 for a quarter to ten. He was in the stateroom until, he says, ten to ten and left him alive and cross.
secrets.testimonySummary: Zippelli admits the Commodore summoned him to the stateroom at a quarter to ten. He says he left at ten to ten, with the Commodore alive and cross.

secrets.description: His trunk's false wall hides 'cargo' in crocks for a dawn handover, and he made the false bottoms.
secrets.testimonySummary: Zippelli admits his trunk's false wall carries 'cargo' in false-bottomed crocks for a dawn handover, and that he made the false bottoms himself.

secrets.description: He bonked the Commodore at 21:52, set the watch, hid the crock, and planned the cheer with the Captain.

relationships.description: The Commodore halved his fee and billed him as THE BRINE DIP. Zippelli calls it 'an insult to the art'.
A fellow professional of the stage and the sea, Zippelli says, and says no more.
She sealed the chest. Zippelli praises her wax seal at every opportunity, since it is his favourite alibi.
The niece applauded loudest. Zippelli finds her charming and easy to dazzle.
The cook brought an omelette. Zippelli would rather not discuss the omelette.

intendedLies.topic: where he was from half past nine
intendedLies.claim: Zippelli was in his greenroom from half past nine until the Plunge, alone with his nerves. Zippelli never sets foot below the saloon deck.

intendedLies.topic: the Commodore's state when he left
intendedLies.claim: Zippelli left him alive and grumpy at ten to ten, then went straight back to the greenroom. He cheered at the shark, didn't he? Ask anyone.
Oranges? Zippelli would sooner kiss a jellyfish. Zippelli has not touched marmalade in ten years: one whiff and he swells like a pufferfish.
That trunk? Ropes, silks, and a rabbit named Mr. Biscuit. Look all you like.

forbiddenPhrases.note: The deed, first or third person.
Before the summons he never admits going below. Narrowed from bare 'stateroom', which his open facts (the trumpet, the sign) use.
The weapon's name in the culprit's mouth, never.
The doer never names his partner in the smuggling.
The detective was seasick in a forward cabin all evening and witnessed nothing.

actions: produces a silk handkerchief from thin air and dabs his moustache
bows low enough to sweep the carpet with his cape
fans out a deck of cards, glances at one, and pockets the lot
tugs his white gloves tighter, finger by finger
strikes a pose as if a spotlight had found him
sneezes theatrically and blames the draught
deflections: Zippelli does not answer questions. Zippelli answers applause.
A magician never reveals. It is in the contract.
Ah, but that is the trick, detective, and the trick is not for sale.
Zippelli has escaped from worse questions than this, chained and underwater.
Nothing up the sleeve, detective. Much.
The Great Zippelli declines, with a flourish.
